claims.text: The target material is a Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy in a solidified solid-solution state.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is an appropriate Co-containing baseline.
CoCrFeMnNi has a single FCC phase thermodynamically stable at temperatures at or above 900 °C.
The Co-containing NiCrFeCoMn alloy exhibits strain-rate-dependent dynamic mechanical behavior whose high-rate mechanism is not yet clear.
Removing Co lowers the activation barrier for a localized stress-induced phase transition.
The deformation-induced transition may take the form of reversible amorphization or another incipient structural change.
Removing Co reduces variability in stacking-fault energy.
The Co-free alloy has a lower threshold for deformation-induced transformation than CoCrFeMnNi.
A localized phase transformation activated under stress facilitates dislocation motion.
The localized phase transformation postpones strain localization.
Facilitated dislocation motion and delayed strain localization allow the Co-free alloy to retain a favorable strength–ductility balance during dynamic loading.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, the Co-free alloy should show transformation onset at a lower temperature and/or strain rate.
Earlier transformation onset should correlate with maintained or enhanced ductility without loss of strength.
The proposed mechanism operates only within a moderate dynamic-loading temperature and strain-rate window.
At very high temperatures or ultra-low strain rates, other deformation modes will dominate and mask the proposed transformation effect.

Paired in-situ tests under identical temperature and strain-rate conditions can distinguish the Co-free alloy from the Co-containing baseline by measuring transformation onset, phase-fraction evolution, and stress–strain response.
Failure to observe either an earlier or distinct transformation onset or a corresponding dynamic mechanical-response difference in the Co-free alloy would falsify the hypothesis.
